newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: U.S. economy strong, but data unusual-Australian PM.
newsitem.headline: U.S. economy strong, but data unusual-Australian PM.

text.p: Australian Prime Minister John Howard said on Monday the U.S. economy was stronger than it had been for some time, but U.S. authorities did not fully understand the unusually good data.
"The mood in America, economically, is very buoyant," Howard told Melbourne radio 3AW from New York.

"The chairman of the Federal Reserve ... Alan Greenspan told me that the sort of numbers they are now getting are virtually unbelievable and he doesn't fully understand all of the reasons, but he sees it."
Howard said the good economic situation in the U.S. was also good for Australia.
"All of the signs are very positive (for Australia)," he said.
Australia's Reserve Bank holds its monthly meeting on Tuesday, with economists increasingly expecting a fifth cut n official cash rates.
The Reserve has cut rates by a total 2.0 percentage points to 5.5 percent in four equal cuts over the past 12 months.
